_doc: Gold cases for the MIGRATED VAULT corpus — a different corpus from eval/gold.json, which
measures the three reference documents (ddia-2e, go-spec, paper-moral). Nothing here reads or
writes out/substrate.db. Run against a composed scope:
substrate eval --db out-vault/scripta.db --gold eval/gold-vault.json \
--baseline eval/.baseline-vault.json
scripta is the scope with the most project notes (15) on top of the 36 inherited core-vault
notes, so one run exercises both tiers and the inheritance path. The core-vault cases
generalise to every other scope, since all six inherit the same core.
METHOD — the constraint that makes these worth running:
Every case was written from the NOTE, read in the vault, never from retrieval output. Cases read
off current output would be tautological — they would confirm whatever the engine already does,
which is the failure eval/gold.json's own header records. Three topics (launchd, Clerk, the
on-device table decision) had been queried by hand in the session that authored this file, so
their behaviour was already known; assertions were still taken from the note text, but they are
the least blind cases here and should be the first suspected if this set ever looks too easy.
SHAPE — deliberately no `doc` and no `expect_doc`:
Both scope the search by an output-directory key, and for vault notes that key carries a content
hash (core-vault__launchd-over-sandbox-schedulers__f06bc63c) which changes on any edit — a case
would silently become 'doc not indexed'. Every case here searches the WHOLE composed scope, and
`path` carries the attribution: it names the note's H1, so only a chunk from the intended note
can satisfy it. 'The right note must win out of 51' is the question a vault corpus poses.
COHORT — assigned by measurement, not by feel:
`_overlap` is the fraction of the query's content words (stopwords and <=3-char tokens removed)
appearing VERBATIM anywhere in the target note. >= 0.75 is `lexical`, below is `semantic`. It is
computed from the query and the note alone, so it cannot be fitted to a result. This matters:
the first 26 cases were hand-labelled and came out 2 lexical / 24 semantic, which put the entire
CI gate — report() gates on the LEXICAL cohort only — on two cases. Measured, the same 26 are 21
lexical / 5 semantic: the questions had been written in the notes' own vocabulary without anyone
intending it. The eight `vault-p-*` cases were then added deliberately paraphrased, to give the
semantic cohort a usable denominator rather than leave it at five.
answer   - a phrase the correct passage must contain. The SEMANTIC gate.
path     - fragments the chunk's structural path must contain. The ATTRIBUTION gate, and here
also the which-note gate.
A case passes only if ONE returned chunk satisfies answer AND path together. Every case was
checked satisfiable against the index before the first run — for each, at least one chunk
carries both gates — so a failure is a retrieval result and never a malformed assertion.
STATUS: only active/complete notes are eligible. The default filter excludes archived and
superseded, so on-device-table-llm-rejected (archived), superseded-decisions and
model-engine-panel-raw (superseded) are absent — a case over them could only fail, and would
measure the filter rather than retrieval.
GATES are DECLARED TARGETS, fixed before the first run and NOT moved after seeing it. If a run
misses them that is a finding about retrieval on this corpus, not a reason to lower the bar.
